DRG turned out to be the most polished and well optimized game I´ve seen release in several years. It seems to be created by people actually playing games themself because it´s a f@ing blast to play, awesome, every minute. Every little perspective of the game is so thought through, satisfying and well working. Strongly recommend if a soft and highly enjoyable co-op, pve game with well balanced teamwork is what you seek!

[h1] Karl Would Approve [/h1]
I've played this game for over 400 hours, for good reason. DRG manages to impressively deliver a multi-layered co-op experience that's just as fun playing with random teams as it is playing with the boys, or even family.

[h1] Pros: [/h1]
+ Low-poly art style looks great, with a lot of charm, all without sacrificing clarity or requiring a high-end PC build.
+ The core gameplay is satisfying, with each class feeling useful and able to impact the mission, yet never so independent as to render the others useless. The procedural layouts, objectives, and enemy design naturally foster cooperation and allow for organic challenges.
+ Music is good if you like sci-fi/synth genres.
+ Even if you don't want to use a mic, or type in chat, the ping system is easy to use and makes communication easy.
+ Four distinct classes, upgrades, alternate weapons, perks, and overclocks allow for each player to define how their dwarves play, with a ton of variability.
+ Tons of cosmetics, with no lootboxes!
+ A fair selling price, plus free updates, plus the only dlc being unique cosmetics means that this is one of the cleanest business models I've seen. Let me be clear: The cosmetic dlc items can't be earned in game, which is actually good because the developers have no incentive to pad the grind.

[h1] Cons: [/h1]
- Mission variety could be better; it's not bad, and the procedural maps help, but it does start feeling same-y after a long time. The developers are actively working on improving mission variety, and recent updates have added new secondary objectives, as well as new primary objectives which feel quite distinct from the already existing types. 
- The only long-term goals in endgame are: unlocking cosmetics, collecting weapon overclocks, raising promotion level, and achievement hunting. The game could stand to get some better endgame rewards, but keep in mind that I've played for 400+ hours, though that feeling of diminishing rewards set in closer to 200 hours.
- The game can still be a bit buggy at times (and not the alien kind). Some examples include: Dangerous enemies like grabbers spawning next to you, or failing to make their warning call, or enemies attacking through thin terrain. This has gotten substantially better with time, but some issues still persist.
- The "Point Extraction" mission type maps seem to be based off of a few templates, with some details like biome type, ore spawns, and biome-specific object placement being random. The problem is that exploration and cave traversal are much less interesting if you already know the layout.

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]
Deep Rock Galactic is a rock-solid game that any fan of cooperative horde-fighters (Payday 2, L4D2, Vermintide, etc.) can get dozens upon dozens of hours of enjoyment out of, but it does have some room for improvement. It's very well priced, and I would recommend this to anyone who enjoys cooperative games.

Such an amazing game, honestly. I can't add much more than what's been said. Co-op, class-based shooter with procedurally generated maps, loads of weapons, customization options, difficulties and more. It''s surprisingly fun alone, I've met a bunch of really awesome people via matchmaking.  Co-op with friends is where it really shines, though. Grab some fellow dwarves, dig deep, lose yourself in the cavernous depths and come out rich. ROCK AND STONE!!
